svg.title: RIEMANN-MASULLO-DIAGRAMS D4 — Chapter 4 · Ch04_PeriodicSchauderBases, declaration by declaration
svg.desc: riemann-masullo at 72a10ff: the 696 declarations of the 90 items on C4, each with its kind, file, line and state; 63 declarations with a Deviation: line, quoted; and the items of other directories each item uses.

g.text: riemann-masullo at 72a10ff: the 696 declarations of the 90 items on C4, each with its kind, file, line and state; 63 declarations with a Deviation: line, quoted; and the items of other directories each item uses.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Posters: M1, what the targets rest on · M2, the steps with no known repair · M3, the paper by depth · M4, every chapter · M5, the refutations. Names, items, files, entries and posters are links, underlined under the pointer: a card's title or a Lean name opens the source at the pin.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: How to read it. The expansion of C4's cards, in the same order: one block per item, its heading opening the card, and under it, in italics, the first sentence of its first declaration's docstring, quoted. Then the declarations whose docstring states how the Lean departs from the print, each with its Deviation: line quoted from the Lean

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: source (Apache-2.0), then every declaration of the item. A name opens its line at the pin. A declaration's state is read from the terms: open when it uses sorryAx, resting when something open is below it. That a declaration states what its Deviation: line says is the docstring's claim, not checked here.

g.text: The Fourier series of a smooth function on the unit circle converges uniformly in every derivative order.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: Functions on the circle are represented by their periodic lifts, and the smooth convergence is expressed using the net of finite partial sums.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: We use periodic lifts and take the symmetric partial sums.

g.text: Logarithmic commensurability of the bases is equivalent to finiteness of all mutual cyclic phases.

g.text: Log-moments of order strictly below the multiplicity vanish on the isotypic difference product, so they descend to the quotient.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: The actual log-periods are commensurate, as required by the finite-phase step (4.6.1.25).

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: The actual log-periods are commensurate (hcomm); ERRATA F235 shows the bound fails without that. A positive multiple of a power of one plus the frequency norm expresses polynomial growth.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: The actual log-periods are commensurate. A positive multiple of a power of one plus the frequency norm expresses polynomial growth.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: The sequence is extended by zero at indices where the moment order is at least the multiplicity, consistent with (4.6.1.15). The page prints "multiplicity at least m", which includes the indices where the order equals the multiplicity; the moment of the test function at those indices is not covered here. The decay estimate does not require commensurability.
